🕶 Review drafts

Games you didn't log, with the result hidden. Rate the draft the way you would have live — that's what makes these usable as training data. If you can see who won, the rating just records the answer and the model learns nothing. The old per-player impact review still exists under Player impact in the menu; it feeds the Player Profiles page.

📺 Watch
Streams play muted — tap 🔇 on a tile to move audio to it. Keeping the logger tab in front means the live feed keeps polling at full speed.
Players black, or "failed to determine content classification"?
That message comes from Twitch's own player when it cannot load the channel's classification data, which usually means something is blocking its background requests. Worth trying, roughly in order:
  • Pause any ad blocker or privacy extension for this site — the usual cause.
  • Allow third-party cookies for twitch.tv; the player keeps its session there.
  • Hit ↻ on a tile to reload just that player.
  • Check the channel is actually live — an offline channel renders black.
  • Open ↗ to confirm the stream plays on Twitch itself.
This is Twitch's player running inside the page, so its restrictions apply exactly as they would on twitch.tv.

League tier weights
Tier weights scale player impact rankings across leagues. International games use the average weight of both teams' home leagues — good performances from weaker leagues are rewarded more, poor performances from stronger leagues penalised more.
🧮 Derive tiers from your data

Rather than guessing, use two bridges that actually connect leagues: players who have appeared in more than one, and international games between them. A player rated 8 in an ERL and 6 in a major says the major is roughly two points harder.

📊 Model Analysis
⚖️ Factor weights

Tune how much each factor can influence predictions. Default 1.0. Reduce a factor if it's consistently driving overconfident wrong predictions. Changes apply immediately.

Full model breakdown

Pick any logged game to see every factor the model considered — including ones that didn't fire — and the exact log-odds contribution of each.

📐 Probability calibration (Platt scaling)

Fits a curve to your prediction outcomes so the model reports honest probabilities. It still ranks the same game as most confident — it just stops inflating the number. This refits automatically every time you log a game, so the button is only needed to force it.

Calibration — how accurate is the model?

When the model says 65%, does the predicted side actually win 65% of the time? Vertical line = expected, bar = actual.

🧠 Is your judgement reaching the model?

Your draft read, skill read and execution read do not go into the prediction directly — each is converted into a historical win rate for games you rated the same way. If that lookup has few games behind it, a strong read contributes almost nothing.

🌡 Recent form

Whether a bad run is the model breaking or ordinary variance. Compares the last 20 predictions against everything before them, with the range you would expect from chance alone.

🧭 Your read — where it works and where it doesn't

Scores the call you made on each game, not the model's. Splits it by the situations where a read tends to go wrong — side, favourite or underdog, league, how sure you were, and how your draft rating compared with your pick.

💰 Edge vs the market

Accuracy is not the bottom line — beating the price is. A 55% hit rate at 1.90 makes money; 60% at 1.50 loses it. This compares how often your bets won against what the odds implied they should.

📋 Live model track record

The real out-of-sample record of the model you actually bet with. Every game you logged stored the prediction the 13-factor model made at the time, before the result was known — so this needs no simulation and cannot leak. This is the number that matters; the backtest below only covers the 5-factor subset.

🧑 You vs the model

Your blinded reads from the review page, scored against the model on exactly the same games. Games you marked as already known are excluded.

🔥 Bet streaks by champion

Champions where your last several bets all lost — either backing them or against them. Shown alongside how many runs chance alone should produce, so you can tell a signal from ordinary variance.

⚖ Swing champions

Tests whether a champion amplifies the gap between teams — winning more than expected when their side is already favoured, and less when it isn't. That is the measurable version of "only good in the better player's hands". Uses actual results rather than model predictions, so it runs on your whole bulk pool.

⚔ Champion reliability

For every champion in your logged games, how well the model did when it was on the board — either side. The question is not whether a champion wins, but whether the model can read games containing it. High overshoot means the model is more overconfident than usual when this champion appears.

👁 Watchlist

Pre-register a suspicion. Only games logged after you add a champion count toward its result, so the hypothesis is fixed before the data exists — which is what makes it a real test rather than a pattern you found by looking.

📉 Where it fails

Splits the same stored predictions by league, and by how much history the model actually had for the teams involved. If the damage is concentrated where training data is thin, the fix is more data — not a different model.

🔬 Backtest

Walk-forward predicts each game using only games played before it — the same information you actually have live. The first button runs the model that actually makes your predictions, on every stored game. Use that number.

REFERENCE MODEL · 5 FACTORS, HAND-LOGGED GAMES ONLY

These run a cut-down model — factors 1, 5, 7, 9 and 12 only, no shrinkage, no calibration — over your hand-logged games rather than the full pool. It is not what predicts your games, so treat its accuracy as a reference point, not a score. Leave-one-out lets each prediction see later games, so it will look better than reality; the gap to walk-forward is how much is borrowed from hindsight.

🧪 Factor diagnostic

Scores each factor on its own, walk-forward. Direction is how often a factor pointed at the eventual winner — below 50% means it is pointing the wrong way. Drop it re-runs the whole backtest with that factor switched off: a positive number there means the model gets better without it.

Factor accuracy

How often each factor you provide actually correlates with the winner across all logged games.

High-confidence failures

Games where you marked High confidence but the other team won — useful for spotting blind spots.

Games where you went against the model's pick. Track record shows whether your instincts or the model are right.

☁ Device sync

Keeps your desktop, laptop and phone on the same data. Every change merges per game, so edits on two devices no longer overwrite each other and deleted games stay deleted.

One-time setup (~10 min, free):
1. Sign in at dash.cloudflare.com (free plan is fine).
2. Open Workers & Pages in the sidebar. Find KV and create a namespace called draft-logger.
3. Back in Workers & Pages → Create → Start with Hello World. Deploy, then Edit code, replace everything with sync-worker.js, Deploy again.
4. On the Worker: Settings → Bindings → Add → KV namespace. Variable name must be exactly SYNC_KV; select draft-logger.
5. Settings → Variables and Secrets → Add, type Secret, name exactly SYNC_CODE, value = any long random string.
6. Copy the Worker's *.workers.dev URL. Paste it and the same secret below, on all three devices.
✓ Everything is saved to the server. Last sync 8/12/2026, 3:30:49 PM.
✈ Going offline

Prepare the app for a trip: sync everything now, and make sure the review queue and champion images are cached so draft rating works with no connection.

Syncs automatically a couple of seconds after any change, when you switch back to the tab, and every 45 seconds while it is open.
📈 Live game states

Records gold, kills, towers, dragons and barons every 45 seconds during live games, then labels each timeline with the result. This is the training data a live win-probability bar would need — the kind of thing a chess engine shows on the side. It reuses the polling already happening, so it adds no network traffic.

0 games · 0 with a known result · 0 snapshots · ~0 KB
Collecting every 180s while the app is open, on any screen, across all leagues — the league filter is not applied here because game state predicts outcomes regardless of league. Needs a few thousand labelled games to fit a model, and cannot be backfilled: the feed only serves live and recent matches.
🔎 Data health

What is actually in your stored games, broken down by source. Tells you whether a re-import would gain anything before you spend time on one.

🧹 Duplicate games

The same match can end up stored twice — imported from two sources, or re-imported after ids changed. Duplicates count twice in training, which quietly inflates whatever they contain.

↩ Import from old JSONBin

One-time recovery. Pulls anything still sitting in your old bin that is not on this device, then pushes the result to the new sync. Existing local games are never overwritten.

↓ Export data

Downloads everything — all logged games, bulk imports, bets, player ratings, tier weights, and bankroll settings — as a JSON file. Use this to move all data to another device.

↑ Import data

Load a previously exported JSON backup. Merges with existing data — nothing is overwritten or deleted.

🔍 Live API debug

Shows exactly what getLive returns — useful for diagnosing missing games.

🔀 Team name aliases

Map old team names to current ones so historical data (rebrands, acquisitions) is counted in the right team's stats and model.

📥 Bulk import past games

Imports completed games from Riot's API to build up model training data. Fetches team names, champion picks, winners, and league for each game. No predictions, bets, or player ratings — those stay yours to add manually.

🐉 LPL historical data (Leaguepedia)

Imports LPL champion pick data from the LoL Esports wiki. Use this to build up LPL champion win rates since the Riot API marks LPL games as completed before they start. Manual fallback only — don't rely on it as primary data.
